questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
So i think that i was incredibly lucky in that the Airbnb host i stayed with was incredibly kind and also offered me to stay in the room that he normally would have rented out to guests. I did though also scour the local market for potential flats, but i ended up staying with my Airbnb host. Also becausee that way i would stay with native speakers of spanish only, which was what i wanted. 
If i were to recommend people going on their first stay abroad, i would recommend being patient. Take your time to find the flat that is suitable for you and the roommates with whom you can develop a friendship with. That is, don't rent a flat because you want to find a place to live as fast as possible, but rather take your time. There is nothing worse than living with people who you can't deal with.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was very different in that the style in Spain seems much more rigid. That is, it seems like they put more en emphasis on a sort of copy paste style of teaching where the students basically notes down everything going on in the class for then later being requiered to being able to answer those questions from memory. A style which is very different from the one in Denmark where it seems that the teachers try and create room for a discussion to be held in class. 
In short:
Spain more rigid, more focus on copy paste style of teaching, few discussions and little involvement from the class
Denmark is more dynamic, more focus on critical thinking, discussions in class so forth

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: go to the ESN meetings, don't be afraid to engage in conversation with the locals, find yourself a gym or a sportscenter and start training, meeting the locals to learn spanish better

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is honestly plenty of places to visit in Extremadura, just ask the locals. They are very friendly and will often give you recommenddations for places to visit or see.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Incredibly easy, but i have been to Spain several times

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just don't be afraid of engaging in conversation with the locals. They are very friendly and will help you. Have a positive attitude

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Obviously not everyone speaks english here so sometimes there can be a language barrier between you and the locals, which is for the better. Then you are forced to speak spanish

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Things seems less stressful here, people are more open and willing to connect with you if you will let them. I have several times been invited out for beer with the locals because we just started talking at the gym or whatever.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Come a little before the beginning of your stay so you can get to know the cty a little and find a place to live. I came a week earlier. 
Make sure you have your MOnline sorted out
relax and have a good time

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sort out the bureaucratic  stuff as early as possible so there is less stress

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to live with my roommates and experiencing the city and what the local people are like here.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The rigid educational system of the universities and my correspondance with the office for exchange students in Cph
